title: Woman at a Well
medium: Etching and aquatint on laid paper; second state of three

altText: A print of a woman at a well, drawn in fine dark lines with soft gray tones.

context: An etching and aquatint by the French artist Camille Pissarro, dated 1891, showing a woman at a well. Pissarro often portrayed country people and everyday rural life.

descriptions.k: A woman stands at a well. A well is a deep hole where people get water. The picture has fine lines and soft gray shading. What do you think she is doing? Why does she need water?
descriptions.g12: Camille Pissarro made this print of a woman at a well in France. Long ago, many people got water from wells. The picture uses thin lines and soft gray patches. Look at the woman and the well. What do you think she is going to do with the water?
descriptions.g35: Camille Pissarro often made art about country life in France. This print from 1891 shows a woman at a well, which was a place where people drew water before many homes had taps. He used etching for thin lines and aquatint for soft, gray areas. Look at where the lines are dark and where they are light. How do they help you picture the place?
descriptions.g68: Pissarro made this print in 1891, part of his long interest in rural life and ordinary work. A well was a daily gathering point for water, so the subject connects to routines and community. He used etching for line and aquatint, which creates soft, grainy tones, and the Met lists this as the second of three states. Notice how line and tone together build the figure and setting. What does the print suggest about daily routines?
descriptions.g910: In Woman at a Well, Pissarro draws on his enduring interest in rural labor and daily routine. Etching provides linear structure while aquatint adds soft tonal areas, a combination that lets the figure and setting emerge from atmosphere rather than outline. The second of three states shows him revising the plate. Pissarro's rural subjects were often presented without sentimentality, though scholars debate how he balanced observation with ideals about work. Consider how the print treats the woman as part of her environment.
descriptions.g1112: Woman at a Well (1891) reflects Pissarro's persistent attention to rural work, a theme he approached with sympathy and, as many scholars note, with an interest in community and labor shaped by his own political outlook. Etching and aquatint combine linear structure with atmospheric tone, and the second of three states reveals a plate in progress. The print offers little narrative, so meaning rests on composition and mood rather than story. How do you weigh its observational quality against the possibility that it idealizes rural life?

teacherNote.context: Camille Pissarro made many images of rural life in France. The Met record dates this print 1891 and lists it as etching and aquatint, second state of three.
directions: Have students shade a drawing with pencil to create gray tones, then compare with line only.
Ask students to compare this print with Wooded Landscape at L'Hermitage (the other Pissarro print in the archive).
Discuss everyday routines that rarely appear in art.
